overview.title: Start
overview.subtitle: What is running, which theme is on and where you are working.
overview.notSetUpText: Setup gets GlazeWM and the other programs straight from their vendors, applies the theme and the shortcuts, and makes a restore point first.
overview.notSetUpLegacy: Winarchy Lite is already in use on this PC. Setup takes over its themes and wallpapers, stops the old shortcut script and removes its autostart entry. All of it can be undone.
overview.programsHint: Every six hours WinMarchy looks for new versions of the programs it installed itself. If something is missing, the setup downloads it straight from the vendor.
overview.workspaceHint: Win+Ctrl+J switches this workspace's layout, Win+K shows every shortcut.
overview.glazeHint: Without GlazeWM there is no tiling and no workspaces. Win+Shift+Alt+R starts it.
overview.versionsNone: WinMarchy has not installed any programs itself yet, so there is nothing to update.
overview.versionsUnknown: No new versions looked up yet.
overview.updateToHint: {tool} closes for a moment, is swapped and starts again.
overview.pauseHint: Windows looks and behaves as without WinMarchy until you resume (also with Win+Alt+Esc). A restart ends the pause.
overview.resumeHint: Shortcuts, GlazeWM, bar, Fluent Search, theme and wallpaper come back.

tools.glazeStopping: Ending GlazeWM for the swap, the windows stay open …

setup.title: Setup
setup.subtitle: Run it once and Windows looks like Omarchy. A restore point comes first, and Undo takes you back at any time.
setup.programsText: Every program comes straight from the vendor's GitHub release and is checked before it is unpacked. Everything goes to C:\WinMarchy\Tools, no admin rights needed.

why.glazewm: Tiles the windows and runs the workspaces. Nothing works without it.
why.autohotkey: Catches the shortcuts, including the Win key on its own.
why.pwsh: PowerShell 7 for the terminal. Windows only ships the old 5.1.
why.herdr: Terminal workspace for coding agents, Win+Ctrl+Enter. Still beta on Windows.
why.pi: The Pi coding agent in the terminal, Win+Alt+Enter.
why.greenshot: Screenshots with an editor, if Snipping Tool is not enough for you. Switch in the settings.
why.yasb: The bar at the top: workspaces, a clock with calendar, sound, Wi-Fi and battery. Small menus drop down from it; you add entries of your own on the Tiling page.
why.starship: Omarchy's prompt for PowerShell: folder, Git branch and status, in the theme's colours. Where Windows PowerShell loads no profiles, WinMarchy ticks PowerShell 7 as well.
why.fastfetch: Shows in every new terminal tab what is inside your computer, with IP and MAC address, like Omarchy's About. Also in the bar's logo menu and under About in the WinMarchy menu.
why.explorerblurmica: Blur behind Explorer in the theme's colour. Registered for your account only; switch it off under Settings.
why.fluentsearch: The launcher behind the Win key, like Walker in Omarchy: search apps, files and settings. Freeware, but not open source.
why.bcuninstaller: Removes programs thoroughly, leftovers in folders and the registry included, several at once. Portable build; without admin rights only for your account.

setup.autostartHint: One entry in the Startup folder. WinMarchy then starts GlazeWM, the bar and the shortcuts.
setup.taskbarHint: The top bar takes over. The taskbar comes back when you quit WinMarchy.
setup.barHint: Workspaces, clock, network, sound and battery, like Waybar in Omarchy.
setup.wallpapersHint: All {count} pictures of the {themes} themes, about {size}. Every theme then has its pictures right away.
setup.startHint: Takes one to three minutes, depending on your connection.
setup.done: All set. Win+K shows every shortcut.
setup.extrasText: Not needed for the Omarchy desktop. You can also install them one by one later.
setup.piNeedsBash: Needs Git Bash, which is missing here.

hotkeys.winAloneHint: Like Super in Omarchy. Ctrl+Esc still opens the Start menu.

hotkeys.unstarTip: No longer a favourite: Win+K lists it under “Optional”

commands.layout: Set the screen's layout (dwindle, columns, scrolling)

commands.focus: Focus in a direction (left, right, up, down)

tiling.title: Tiling
tiling.subtitle: How GlazeWM arranges your windows. Each screen has its layout, and every workspace on it follows.
tiling.scrollingNote: Scrolling puts the windows side by side as columns in a row that may be wider than the screen; two columns are in view. Win+Left and Right scroll, Win+Shift+Arrow moves the column, at the end of the row onto the screen next to it. Columns off the screen wait out of sight until the row scrolls to them. GlazeWM cannot do this itself, so WinMarchy places these windows (they float for it).
tiling.dimHint: Windows without focus become slightly see-through.
tiling.taskbarHint: Comes back as soon as you quit WinMarchy.
tiling.applyHint: Rewrites the GlazeWM config and reloads it. A restore point comes first.
tiling.splitNext: The split applies from the next window on.
tiling.monitorsText: As in Omarchy's Screens plugin: each screen gets its layout and fixed workspaces. Win+3 always opens workspace 3 on its screen and in that screen's layout, and a work mode only takes that screen's workspaces there.
tiling.monitorsHint: Screens are listed from left to right, the way they are arranged in Windows Settings under Display; GlazeWM counts them the same way. Unplug one and its workspaces move to another. Its row stays here until you clear it, so the split fits again at the dock.
tiling.monitorsInvalid: {name}: only workspace numbers from 1 to 6, such as 1-2 or 3, 4.
tiling.monitorsTwice: Workspace {workspace} is listed for {a} and for {b}. Each workspace belongs to one screen.
tiling.monitorWorkspacesHint: For example 1-2 or 3, 4. There are six workspaces, five on a single screen. Empty: this screen takes whatever is free.
tiling.desktopAppLate: {action} showed no window within 12 seconds; it was meant for workspace {workspace}.
tiling.monitorsFailed: Could not move workspaces to their monitors: {detail}
tiling.shortcutsHint: They sit in the menu under the logo, which drops down from the top; with “As button” also right in the bar. Write the action as for a shortcut: app:terminal, web:https://…, open:ms-settings:…, do:theme-menu or run:C:\Path\script.ps1. YASB only.
tiling.shortcutNoTitle: The entry with the action {action} needs a name.
tiling.newWindowEndsFullscreen: A new window ends full screen
tiling.newWindowEndsFullscreenHint: When a window opens next to one in full screen or a program pushes in front of it, that one goes back into its tile, as in Hyprland. It gets its full screen back once the other one closes or you return to it.
tiling.workModesText: One key press gives every monitor a fresh workspace and opens the mode's programs there, for research, say, or for the tools of the work at hand. Open windows stay on their workspaces. If the mode is running already, the key brings it back and starts only what you closed. Press it again while in the mode and what was on the screens before comes back.
tiling.workModesHint: One program per monitor. If a monitor is missing, its program goes to the last one that is connected. On a single monitor all of the mode's programs share it, in the dwindle layout. The browser takes addresses and opens them as the tabs of a new window: app:browser https://page-one.com https://page-two.com
tiling.workModeNameHint: Shown in the notice when switching. Empty: work mode 1, 2 or 3.
tiling.workModeAppHint: What starts here, written like a shortcut's action. Empty: nothing.
tiling.layoutsText: Which layout a screen has is set below with the screens. Win+Ctrl+J moves the screen you are on to the next one: dwindle, columns, scrolling.
tiling.floatingNote: Floating is not a layout: Win+T takes a single window out, it then floats above the tiles and nothing covers it. Win+T again puts it back into the screen's layout. Win+O puts it small into the bottom right corner.
tiling.layoutsFailed: The screens' layouts could not be applied: {detail}
tiling.unsavedText: Something on the Tiling page is changed but not applied yet.
tiling.mainScreenHint: Gets workspaces 1 and 2. When you pick another one, the other screens share the rest evenly.
tiling.monitorsSuggested: Nothing is set yet, so this is the suggestion: the main screen gets 1 and 2, the others the rest. "Apply" makes it stick. Screens count from left to right, the way GlazeWM counts them.
tiling.workspaceLimit: There is no workspace {number}. There are {count} workspaces.
tiling.workspaceLimitOne: There is no workspace {number} on a single screen. There are {count} here, six from the second screen on.

layouts.dwindleText: Each new window splits the space of the focused one. Omarchy's default.
layouts.columnsText: Windows side by side, equally wide.
layouts.scrollingText: Columns in a row, wider than the screen. Win+Arrow scrolls.
layouts.floatingGone: The floating layout is gone. The windows of workspace {workspaces} are tiled again; single windows float with Win+T.

scratchpad.stored: In the scratchpad. Win+S shows it, Win+Alt+S on it takes it back out.
scratchpad.empty: The scratchpad is empty. Win+Alt+S puts a window in.
scratchpad.recovered: Brought {count} windows from hidden workspaces back to workspace {workspace}.

restore.title: Undo
restore.subtitle: Before WinMarchy changes anything, it saves the old state. Here you undo single changes or all of them.
restore.originalText: WinMarchy changed {count} things since {date}. This puts all of them back the way they were.
restore.nothingYet: WinMarchy has not changed anything yet.
restore.noTools: WinMarchy has not installed any programs.
restore.confirmAll: {count} files and settings go back to how they were before WinMarchy. The bar and the shortcut script stop, the taskbar comes back.
restore.confirmAllTools: The programs in C:\WinMarchy\Tools are deleted.
restore.allDone: Everything is back to how it was before WinMarchy.
restore.confirmPoint: “{title}” sets {count} files and settings back to how they were before.
restore.confirmDelete: “{title}” cannot be restored afterwards. The state before WinMarchy is kept.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Saved in {path}
settings.languageHint: Takes effect the next time WinMarchy starts.
settings.prerelease: Test build, does not update itself
settings.autoUpdateHint: WinMarchy downloads new versions from GitHub, checks them and swaps itself when the window is closed. GlazeWM is updated too whenever WinMarchy starts.
settings.filesPathHint: Only needed when WinMarchy cannot find the file itself.
settings.unreadable: Could not read the settings, WinMarchy starts with the defaults: {detail}
settings.fileManagerText: Omarchy opens folders in Nautilus, WinMarchy in Files if you like. This PC, the recycle bin and the control panel stay with Explorer.
settings.filesDefault: Files as the default file manager
settings.filesDefaultHint: Folders, drives and Win+E open Files. Switching it off brings Explorer back, and so does Undo.
settings.filesDefaultMissing: Files is not installed. It is free in the Microsoft Store and at files.community.
settings.filesDefaultOn: Files is now the default file manager.
settings.filesDefaultOff: Explorer is the default file manager again.
settings.browsersText: Two shortcuts, two browsers: Edge for work and Firefox for the rest, for example. Web apps like Spotify open in the first one if it is based on Chromium, else in Edge.
settings.screenshotsText: Omarchy puts the screenshot on the Print key. Here you choose who takes it: Windows' Snipping Tool or Greenshot with its editor.
settings.screenshotWindowsHint: Print and Win+Ctrl+Alt+C open Snipping Tool, Alt+Print records the screen as a video.
settings.screenshotGreenshotHint: Print captures a region, Alt+Print a window, Ctrl+Print the whole screen, as Greenshot is set up. Win+Ctrl+Alt+C works too. The picture is in the clipboard right away, and a small menu offers to save or edit it.
settings.screenshotGreenshotInstall: When you switch, WinMarchy downloads Greenshot straight from its maker.
settings.glazeText: GlazeWM manages the windows. WinMarchy uses its own build for that: GlazeWM from glzr-io with the fixes and features WinMarchy needs (github.com/PixelShober/glazewm). It is not signed and so runs without UIAccess: it does not tile programs that run as administrator.
settings.glazeDone: GlazeWM now runs as the WinMarchy build.
settings.explorerBlurText: Blur behind Explorer, tinted with the theme. Explorer loads a DLL for it; WinMarchy registers it for your account only, without admin rights, and switching it off undoes that. Experimental: a Windows update can break it, and some companies only allow Explorer extensions registered for all users.
settings.explorerBlurConfirm: WinMarchy downloads ExplorerBlurMica from GitHub (Maplespe/ExplorerBlurMica), checks its checksum and registers the DLL for your account. Explorer windows you open then show the effect. If Explorer crashes afterwards: hold Esc while opening Explorer to keep the effect out, and switch it off here.
settings.explorerBlurOnHint: On. The tint follows the theme; new Explorer windows show it.
settings.explorerBlurOffHint: Off. Switching it on downloads ExplorerBlurMica if it is missing.
settings.explorerBlurOn: ExplorerBlurMica is on. Open a new Explorer window.
settings.explorerBlurOff: ExplorerBlurMica is off. It is fully gone after the next sign-in.
settings.glazeOfficialFound: Found: an official release ({path}). It lacks what WinMarchy needs. The button installs the WinMarchy build into C:\WinMarchy\Tools and starts it instead. The official one stays installed but no longer runs.
settings.languageText: Language of this window, the WinMarchy menu and the messages.

log.title: Log
log.subtitle: What WinMarchy did. The files are in {path} and kept for 30 days.
log.policiesHint: Looks for group policies and Intune settings that override WinMarchy.
log.diagnoseHint: Writes what WinMarchy sees right now into a file: GlazeWM, screens, Fluent Search, taskbar, bar, shortcuts. No window titles.
log.verboseHint: For troubleshooting: every shortcut, every GlazeWM command and what Fluent Search, the taskbar, the scratchpad, scrolling and the work modes do. Shown under "All". When you switch it off, today's log file goes to the clipboard and its folder opens.
log.verboseOffCopied: Verbose logging is off. {file} is in the clipboard and its folder is open.
log.verboseOffOpened: Verbose logging is off. The folder with {file} is open; the file could not go to the clipboard.

jobs.filesDefaultOff: Explorer as the default file manager

agent.started: WinMarchy {version} is running in the background
agent.glazeMissing: GlazeWM is not installed, tiling stays off.
agent.startFailed: Something went wrong while starting the programs: {detail}
agent.taskbarSettingOff: The taskbar is not hidden in the first place. Turn that on under Tiling.
agent.awakeOn: Staying awake. Screen and PC will not go to sleep.
agent.noWallpapers: No wallpapers downloaded for this theme yet.
agent.restored: Everything reset. WinMarchy stays in the notification area until you quit it.
agent.glazeConnectFailed: GlazeWM is running, but WinMarchy cannot reach it: {detail}
agent.glazeReconnecting: The connection to GlazeWM was stuck, GlazeWM itself answers. WinMarchy connects again.
agent.glazeHung: GlazeWM has not answered any command for more than ten seconds. WinMarchy restarts it.
agent.glazeRestarting: GlazeWM hung and restarts. Your windows stay open.
agent.glazeHungAgain: GlazeWM hangs again. “Reload GlazeWM” in the tray menu restarts it; the log shows what happened before.
agent.glazeOtherEnded: Another GlazeWM ran instead of the WinMarchy build ({path}). WinMarchy ended it and starts its own.
agent.greenshotTakesOver: Screenshots now go through Greenshot: the picture is in the clipboard right away, and a menu offers to save it.
agent.glazeStillRunning: The old GlazeWM does not end, so no new one starts.
agent.glazeNoAnswerAfterStart: GlazeWM does not answer 20 seconds after starting. Its error log says: {detail}
agent.glazeNoErrors: nothing new (errors.log has no entries from that time)
agent.glazeStillDown: GlazeWM does not answer after a second start either. What GlazeWM reports about it is in the log.
agent.glazeQuit: GlazeWM was quit from its own menu. WinMarchy does not start it by itself; "Reload GlazeWM" (Win+Shift+Alt+R or WinMarchy menu → Update) starts it again.
agent.glazeCrashed: GlazeWM crashed (code {code}), WinMarchy starts it again. Its error log says: {detail}
agent.glazeRestartingCrash: GlazeWM crashed and starts again. Your windows stay open.
agent.glazeCrashesTooOften: GlazeWM crashed three times in ten minutes (last code {code}). WinMarchy no longer starts it by itself; "Reload GlazeWM" starts it again.
agent.glazeBusyAfterWake: GlazeWM does not answer right now. The PC just woke up, was unlocked or changed its screens; WinMarchy waits up to a minute before restarting GlazeWM.
agent.glazeUpkeepFailed: GlazeWM could not be updated at start: {detail}
agent.glazeHungDetail: GlazeWM {version} hung. Its error log says: {detail}
agent.launcherRestarted: Fluent Search was no longer running and has been started again.

effects.colorsLocked: Colours and theme are locked. Light, dark and the Windows accent colour stay as IT sets them.

effects.proxyScript: A proxy script is set ({value}). Downloads from GitHub go through it.

workModes.unknown: There is no work mode “{mode}”, only 1 to 3.
